question:
A 33-year-old male presents to the emergency department with urinary incontinence for the past 6
hours and progressive bilateral weakness and tingling in all extremities for 7 days. His medical history
includes a mild respiratory infection one month ago. He has no significant personal or family medical
history. He reports having two sexual partners and inconsistent condom use. He consumes alcohol
occasionally, is a former smoker who quit one year ago, and denies illicit drug use. His vital signs are
stable and he is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals: - Intact cranial nerves - Muscle
strength 3/5 in all extremities - Positive Babinski sign - Hyperactive deep tendon reflexes (3+) -
Decreased sensation to multiple modalities below the clavicle - Normal cardiopulmonary and
abdominal examinations Which additional finding would most likely be present in this patient? Answer
Choices: (A) Elevated oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid (B) Elevated creatine kinase levels (C)
Anti-ganglioside antibodies in serum (D) Abnormal nerve root potentials on EMG (E) Pleocytosis on

cerebrospinal fluid analysis (F) Positive titers on a rapid plasma reagin test (G) Demyelinating lesions
on brain MRI (H) Positive anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies (I) Anterior nerve root enhancement on
spinal MRI (J) Decreased peripheral nerve conduction velocity on an electrophysiological examination
 A. Elevated creatine kinase levels
B. Anterior nerve root enhancement on spinal MRI
C. Demyelinating lesions on brain MRI
D. Elevated oligoclonal bands in cerebrospinal fluid
E. Anti-ganglioside antibodies in serum
F. Abnormal nerve root potentials on EMG
G. Positive titers on a rapid plasma reagin test
H. Positive anti-acetylcholine receptor antibodies
I. Pleocytosis on cerebrospinal fluid analysis
J. Decreased peripheral nerve conduction velocity on an electrophysiological examination
